sections.section_name: Section A - Objective Type / MCQs / True-False

questions.question_text: In the context of a Confusion Matrix, what does the term 'False Positive' represent?
options: A) The model correctly predicted a positive outcome.
B) The model predicted a positive outcome, but the actual reality was negative.
C) The model predicted a negative outcome, but the actual reality was positive.
D) The model correctly predicted a negative outcome.
questions.answer: B) The model predicted a positive outcome, but the actual reality was negative.

questions.question_text: Which Natural Language Processing (NLP) technique represents text as a mathematical vector based on the frequency of word occurrences, ignoring grammar and order?
True or False: In Computer Vision, 'Semantic Segmentation' involves classifying every single pixel in an image to belong to a specific predefined class (e.g., road, car, pedestrian).
What is the primary formula used to calculate the 'F1 Score' in AI evaluation frameworks?
During text normalization in NLP, which process trims words down to their root form by cutting off prefixes and suffixes (e.g., 'running' becomes 'run')?
True or False: Recall is a better metric than Precision when the cost of False Negatives is extremely high, such as in cancer detection models.
In a grayscale image represented as a digital matrix, what does a pixel value of '0' typically indicate?
Which AI metric measures the ratio of correctly predicted positive observations to the total predicted positive observations?
What does TF-IDF stand for in the context of Natural Language Processing?
In Computer Vision, which task involves drawing bounding boxes around identified objects and labeling them within an image?
Define the term 'Tokenization' as used in Natural Language Processing text preparation pipelines. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Tokenization is the initial NLP step where a long string of continuous text is divided into smaller, individual, manageable units called tokens, such as words or sentences.

questions.question_text: Explain the fundamental difference between Image Classification and Object Detection in computer vision models. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Image Classification assigns a single label to an entire image, whereas Object Detection locates multiple objects within an image and draws bounding boxes around each specific entity.

questions.question_text: Why is the removal of 'stop words' considered necessary before generating a Bag-of-Words vector? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Stop words like 'is', 'the', and 'a' occur frequently but carry no significant semantic meaning. Removing them reduces noise, decreases dataset size, and improves model focus on relevant keywords.

questions.question_text: Describe a scenario where achieving high 'Precision' is prioritized over high 'Recall'. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: High precision is crucial in email spam filtering. A False Positive (flagging a vital email as spam) is highly disruptive, so the model must only predict spam when absolutely certain.

questions.question_text: What does a 'Confusion Matrix' evaluate, and how is its basic layout structured? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A Confusion Matrix evaluates the performance of a classification model. It is typically structured as a 2x2 grid displaying True Positives, True Negatives, False Positives, and False Negatives.

sections.section_name: Section C - Short Answer Application Problems

questions.question_text: A tech company builds a computer vision system to detect unauthorized vehicles in a secure parking zone. Explain how grayscale conversion and edge detection filters work together in the image processing pipeline to identify license plates. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: First, the system converts colored camera feeds into grayscale, reducing computational load by transforming RGB values into single-intensity pixels. Then, edge detection filters apply mathematical kernels to highlight sharp intensity changes, outlining the rectangular shapes and text features characteristic of license plates for final extraction.

questions.question_text: Given the corpus containing two documents: D1='The cat sat on the mat' and D2='The dog sat on the log'. Construct the vocabulary list and write the Bag-of-Words vector array for Document D1. (Assume all text is lowercased). [40-50 words]
questions.answer: First, the combined unique vocabulary list is: [the, cat, sat, on, mat, dog, log]. Using this ordered feature list, the Bag-of-Words frequency vector for D1 maps to: [2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0], indicating two occurrences of 'the', one of 'cat', 'sat', 'on', 'mat', and zero for 'dog' and 'log'.

sections.section_name: Section D - Long Answer / Case-Based Technical Scenarios

questions.question_text: Read the following case context: A bank deploys an AI classification model to predict fraudulent credit card transactions. Out of 1000 total transactions processed, 50 were actually fraudulent. The model flagged 60 transactions as fraudulent. Upon review, 40 of those flagged were true frauds, and 20 were legitimate purchases falsely flagged. Calculate the True Positives, False Positives, True Negatives, and False Negatives. Then, compute the Precision and Recall percentages for this fraud detection system. [60-80 words]
questions.answer: True Positives (actual frauds flagged) = 40. False Positives (legitimate flagged as fraud) = 20. False Negatives (actual frauds missed) = Total actual frauds (50) - TP (40) = 10. True Negatives (legitimate correctly passed) = Total (1000) - Actual Frauds (50) - FP (20) = 930. Precision = TP / (TP + FP) = 40 / 60 = 66.6%. Recall = TP / (TP + FN) = 40 / 50 = 80.0%.

questions.question_text: Read the following case context: An AI customer service chatbot relies heavily on text normalization to understand user queries. A user types: 'Are my shipping deliveries arriving tomorrow???'. Detail the step-by-step NLP text normalization pipeline required to process this raw string into an analysis-ready format, specifically explaining lowercasing, punctuation removal, tokenization, and lemmatization. [60-80 words]
questions.answer: First, lowercasing converts the string to 'are my shipping deliveries arriving tomorrow???'. Next, punctuation removal strips the symbols, leaving 'are my shipping deliveries arriving tomorrow'. Then, tokenization splits it into an array: ['are', 'my', 'shipping', 'deliveries', 'arriving', 'tomorrow']. Finally, lemmatization reduces tokens to their dictionary base forms, transforming 'deliveries' to 'delivery' and 'arriving' to 'arrive', producing a clean, standardized list ready for the intent-matching algorithm.
